units.leftText: but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
units.rightText: But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

units.leftText: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
units.rightText: If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
rightNotes: 5:29 Greek Gehenna; also in verse 30

units.leftText: If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
units.rightText: And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than for your whole body to depart into hell.

units.leftText: “It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
units.rightText: It has also been said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’
rightNotes: 5:31 Deuteronomy 24:1|DEU 24:1*

units.leftText: but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
units.rightText: But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, brings adultery upon her. And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
rightNotes: 5:32 Or causes her to commit adultery

units.leftText: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
units.rightText: Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients, ‘Do not break your oath, but fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
rightNotes: 5:33 Numbers 30:2|NUM 30:2*

units.leftText: but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
units.rightText: But I tell you not to swear at all: either by heaven, for it is God’s throne;

units.leftText: nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
units.rightText: or by the earth, for it is His footstool; or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.

units.leftText: Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
units.rightText: Nor should you swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.

units.leftText: But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
units.rightText: Simply let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’ Anything more comes from the evil one.
rightNotes: 5:37 Or from evil

units.leftText: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
units.rightText: You have heard that it was said, ‘Eye for eye and tooth for tooth.’
rightNotes: 5:38 Exodus 21:24|EXO 21:24*; Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21

units.leftText: But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
units.rightText: But I tell you not to resist an evil person. If someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;

units.leftText: If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
units.rightText: if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;

units.leftText: Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
units.rightText: and if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two miles.
rightNotes: 5:41 Greek one milion; that is, a Roman mile, approximately 4,855 feet or 1,480 meters
5:41 Literally go with him two.

units.leftText: Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
units.rightText: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.

units.leftText: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
units.rightText: You have heard that it was said, ‘Love your neighbor’ and ‘Hate your enemy.’
leftNotes: 5:43 not in the Bible, but see Qumran Manual of Discipline Ix, 21-26
rightNotes: 5:43 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
units.rightText: But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
rightNotes: 5:44 BYZ and TR love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who spitefully accuse you and persecute you; see Luke 6:27–28|LUK 6:27-28*.

units.leftText: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
units.rightText: that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. He causes His sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.

units.leftText: For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
units.rightText: If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Do not even tax collectors do the same?

units.leftText: If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
units.rightText: And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing more than others? Do not even Gentiles do the same?

units.leftText: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
units.rightText: Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.[’’]

units.leftText: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
leftNotes: 6:1 NU reads “acts of righteousness” instead of “charitable giving”
rightNotes: 6:1 BYZ and TR charitable acts or alms

units.leftText: Therefore, when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

units.leftText: But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
units.rightText: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,

units.leftText: so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
units.rightText: so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

units.leftText: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

units.leftText: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
units.rightText: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

units.leftText: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
units.rightText: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need before you ask him.
units.rightText: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.

units.leftText: Pray like this:
units.rightText: So then, this is how you should pray:

units.leftText: Let your Kingdom come.
units.rightText: Your kingdom come,

units.leftText: Give us today our daily bread.
units.rightText: Give us this day our daily bread.

units.leftText: Forgive us our debts,
units.rightText: And forgive us our debts,

units.leftText: Bring us not into temptation,
units.rightText: And lead us not into temptation,

units.leftText: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
units.rightText: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

units.leftText: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
units.rightText: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.

units.leftText: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
units.rightText: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.

units.leftText: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
units.rightText: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,

units.leftText: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
units.rightText: so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.

units.leftText: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
units.rightText: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
rightNotes: 6:19 Or worm; also in verse 20

units.leftText: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
units.rightText: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

units.leftText: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
units.rightText: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

units.leftText: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
units.rightText: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
rightNotes: 6:22 Literally If your eye is sound; see Proverbs 22:9|PRO 22:9*

units.leftText: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
units.rightText: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
rightNotes: 6:23 Literally if your eye is evil; see Proverbs 23:6|PRO 23:6* and Proverbs 28:22

units.leftText: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
units.rightText: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
units.rightText: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

units.leftText: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
units.rightText: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?

units.leftText: “Which of you by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
units.rightText: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
rightNotes: 6:27 Or a single cubit to his height; a cubit was approximately 18 inches or 45 centimeters.

units.leftText: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
units.rightText: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.

units.leftText: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
units.rightText: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.

units.leftText: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
units.rightText: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?

units.leftText: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
units.rightText: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’

units.leftText: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
units.rightText: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.

units.leftText: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
units.rightText: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.
rightNotes: 6:33 SBL, WH, and NE seek first His kingdom; see also Luke 12:31|LUK 12:31*.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
units.rightText: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.[’’]

units.leftText: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
units.rightText: “Do not judge, or you will be judged.

units.leftText: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
units.rightText: For with the same judgment you pronounce, you will be judged, and with the measure you use, it will be measured to you.

units.leftText: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
units.rightText: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

units.leftText: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
units.rightText: How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while there is still a beam in your own eye?

units.leftText: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
units.rightText: You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.

units.leftText: “Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
units.rightText: Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine. If you do, they may trample them under their feet, and then turn and tear you to pieces.

units.leftText: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
units.rightText: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

units.leftText: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
units.rightText: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

units.leftText: Or who is there among you who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
units.rightText: Which of you, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone?

units.leftText: Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
units.rightText: Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?

units.leftText: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
units.rightText: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him!

units.leftText: Therefore, whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
units.rightText: In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you. For this is the essence of the Law and the Prophets.

units.leftText: “Enter in by the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter in by it.
units.rightText: Enter through the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many enter through it.

units.leftText: How narrow is the gate and the way is restricted that leads to life! There are few who find it.
units.rightText: But small is the gate and narrow the way that leads to life, and only a few find it.

units.leftText: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
units.rightText: Beware of false prophets. They come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves.

units.leftText: By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
units.rightText: By their fruit you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?

units.leftText: Even so, every good tree produces good fruit, but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
units.rightText: Likewise, every good tree bears good fruit, but a bad tree bears bad fruit.

units.leftText: A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
units.rightText: A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, and a bad tree cannot bear good fruit.

units.leftText: Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
units.rightText: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.

units.leftText: Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
units.rightText: So then, by their fruit you will recognize them.

units.leftText: “Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven, but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only he who does the will of My Father in heaven.

units.leftText: Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
units.rightText: Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’

units.leftText: Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
units.rightText: Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you workers of lawlessness!’

units.leftText: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine and does them, I will liken him to a wise man who built his house on the rock.
units.rightText: Therefore everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

units.leftText: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
units.rightText: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because its foundation was on the rock.

units.leftText: Everyone who hears these words of mine and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
units.rightText: But everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

units.leftText: The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house; and it fell—and its fall was great.”
units.rightText: The rain fell, the torrents raged, and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell— and great was its collapse!”

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,
units.rightText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, the crowds were astonished at His teaching,

units.leftText: for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.
units.rightText: because He taught as one who had authority, and not as their scribes.

units.leftText: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
units.rightText: When Jesus came down from the mountain, large crowds followed Him.

units.leftText: Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
units.rightText: Suddenly a leper came and knelt before Him, saying, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
rightNotes: 8:2 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
units.rightText: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “See that you tell nobody; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
units.rightText: Then Jesus instructed him, “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and offer the gift prescribed by Moses, as a testimony to them.”
rightNotes: 8:4 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him for help,
units.rightText: When Jesus had entered Capernaum, a centurion came and pleaded with Him,

units.leftText: saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
units.rightText: “Lord, my servant lies at home, paralyzed and in terrible agony.”
rightNotes: 8:6 Or child; also in verses 8 and 13

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
units.rightText: “I will go and heal him,” Jesus replied.

units.leftText: The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
units.rightText: The centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy to have You come under my roof. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

units.leftText: For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
units.rightText: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

units.leftText: When Jesus heard it, he marveled and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
units.rightText: When Jesus heard this, He marveled and said to those following Him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found anyone in Israel with such great faith.

units.leftText: I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,
units.rightText: I say to you that many will come from the east and the west to share the banquet with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
units.rightText: But the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”

units.leftText: Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to the centurion, “Go! As you have believed, so will it be done for you.” And his servant was healed at that very hour.

units.leftText: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.
units.rightText: When Jesus arrived at Peter’s house, He saw Peter’s mother-in-law sick in bed with a fever.

units.leftText: He touched her hand, and the fever left her. So she got up and served him.
units.rightText: So He touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve Him.

units.leftText: When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick,
units.rightText: When evening came, many who were demon-possessed were brought to Jesus, and He drove out the spirits with a word and healed all the sick.

units.leftText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.”
units.rightText: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:

units.leftText: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.
units.rightText: When Jesus saw a large crowd around Him, He gave orders to cross to the other side of the sea.
rightNotes: 8:18 That is, the Sea of Galilee; Greek to the other side

units.leftText: A scribe came and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
units.rightText: And one of the scribes came to Him and said, “Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go.”

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
units.rightText: Jesus replied, “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.”

units.leftText: Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
units.rightText: Another of His disciples requested, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”

units.leftText: But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
units.rightText: But Jesus told him, “Follow Me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”

units.leftText: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
units.rightText: When He got into the boat, His disciples followed Him.

units.leftText: Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves; but he was asleep.
units.rightText: Suddenly a violent storm came up on the sea, so that the boat was engulfed by the waves. But Jesus was sleeping.

units.leftText: The disciples came to him and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”
units.rightText: The disciples went and woke Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?” Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
units.rightText: “You of little faith,” Jesus replied, “why are you so afraid?” Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm.

units.leftText: The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
units.rightText: The men were amazed and asked, “What kind of man is this? Even the winds and the sea obey Him!”

units.leftText: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes, two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.
units.rightText: When Jesus arrived on the other side in the region of the Gadarenes, He was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs. They were so violent that no one could pass that way.
rightNotes: 8:28 BYZ, TR, and PT Gergesenes; other manuscripts Gerasenes

units.leftText: Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”
units.rightText: “What do You want with us, Son of God?” they shouted. “Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?”

units.leftText: Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.
units.rightText: In the distance a large herd of pigs was feeding.

units.leftText: The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”
units.rightText: So the demons begged Jesus, “If You drive us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Go!”
units.rightText: “Go!” He told them. So they came out and went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.

units.leftText: Those who fed them fled and went away into the city and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.
units.rightText: Those tending the pigs ran off into the town and reported all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men.

units.leftText: Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.
units.rightText: Then the whole town went out to meet Jesus. And when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their region.

units.rightText: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to His own town.

units.rightText: As Jesus went on from there, He saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Matthew got up and followed Him.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick do.

units.leftText: But you go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ for I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

units.rightText: Neither do men pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins will burst, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined. Instead, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”

units.leftText: While he told these things to them, behold, a ruler came and worshiped him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
units.rightText: While Jesus was saying these things, a synagogue leader came and knelt before Him. “My daughter has just died,” he said. “But come and place Your hand on her, and she will live.”

units.leftText: Jesus got up and followed him, as did his disciples.

units.leftText: The report of this went out into all that land.
units.rightText: And the news about this spread throughout that region.

units.leftText: As Jesus passed by from there, two blind men followed him, calling out and saying, “Have mercy on us, son of David!”
units.rightText: As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed Him, crying out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”

units.rightText: After Jesus had entered the house, the blind men came to Him. “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” He asked.

units.rightText: Then He touched their eyes and said, “According to your faith will it be done to you.”

units.rightText: And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, “See that no one finds out about this!”

units.leftText: But they went out and spread abroad his fame in all that land.
units.rightText: But they went out and spread the news about Him throughout the land.

units.leftText: As they went out, behold, a mute man who was demon possessed was brought to him.
units.rightText: As they were leaving, a demon-possessed man who was mute was brought to Jesus.

units.leftText: When the demon was cast out, the mute man spoke. The multitudes marveled, saying, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”
units.rightText: And when the demon had been driven out, the man began to speak. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel!”

units.leftText: But the Pharisees said, “By the prince of the demons, he casts out demons.”
units.rightText: But the Pharisees said, “It is by the prince of demons that He drives out demons.”

units.leftText: Jesus went about all the cities and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
units.rightText: Jesus went through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness.

units.leftText: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
units.rightText: When He saw the crowds, He was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.

units.leftText: Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.
units.rightText: Then He said to His disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.

units.leftText: Pray therefore that the Lord of the harvest will send out laborers into his harvest.”
units.rightText: Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest.”

units.leftText: He called to himself his twelve disciples, and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every disease and every sickness.
units.rightText: And calling His twelve disciples to Him, Jesus gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness.

units.leftText: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these. The first, Simon, who is called Peter; Andrew, his brother; James the son of Zebedee; John, his brother;
units.rightText: These are the names of the twelve apostles: first Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew; James son of Zebedee, and his brother John;

units.leftText: Philip; Bartholomew; Thomas; Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus;

units.leftText: Jesus sent these twelve out and commanded them, saying, “Don’t go among the Gentiles, and don’t enter into any city of the Samaritans.
units.rightText: These twelve Jesus sent out with the following instructions: “Do not go onto the road of the Gentiles or enter any town of the Samaritans.

units.leftText: Rather, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
units.rightText: Go rather to the lost sheep of Israel.

units.leftText: As you go, preach, saying, ‘The Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!’
units.rightText: As you go, preach this message: ‘The kingdom of heaven is near.’

units.leftText: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.
units.rightText: Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. Freely you have received; freely give.
rightNotes: 10:8 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: Don’t take any gold, silver, or brass in your money belts.
units.rightText: Do not take along any gold or silver or copper in your belts.

units.leftText: Take no bag for your journey, neither two coats, nor sandals, nor staff: for the laborer is worthy of his food.
units.rightText: Take no bag for the road, or second tunic, or sandals, or staff; for the worker is worthy of his provisions.

units.leftText: Into whatever city or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you go on.
units.rightText: Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there and stay at his house until you move on.
rightNotes: 10:11 Literally stay there

units.leftText: As you enter into the household, greet it.
units.rightText: As you enter the home, greet its occupants.
rightNotes: 10:12 Literally greet it

units.leftText: If the household is worthy, let your peace come on it, but if it isn’t worthy, let your peace return to you.
units.rightText: If the home is worthy, let your peace rest on it, but if it is not, let your peace return to you.

units.leftText: Whoever doesn’t receive you or hear your words, as you go out of that house or that city, shake the dust off your feet.
units.rightText: And if anyone will not welcome you or heed your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.

units.leftText: “Behold, I send you out as sheep among wolves. Therefore be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.
units.rightText: Behold, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves.

units.leftText: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils, and in their synagogues they will scourge you.
units.rightText: But beware of men, for they will hand you over to their councils and flog you in their synagogues.

units.leftText: Yes, and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and to the nations.
units.rightText: On My account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: But when they deliver you up, don’t be anxious how or what you will say, for it will be given you in that hour what you will say.
units.rightText: But when they hand you over, do not worry about how to respond or what to say. In that hour you will be given what to say.

units.leftText: For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you.
units.rightText: For it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.

units.leftText: “Brother will deliver up brother to death, and the father his child. Children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
units.rightText: Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise against their parents and have them put to death.

units.leftText: You will be hated by all men for my name’s sake, but he who endures to the end will be saved.
units.rightText: You will be hated by everyone because of My name, but the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

units.leftText: But when they persecute you in this city, flee into the next, for most certainly I tell you, you will not have gone through the cities of Israel until the Son of Man has come.
units.rightText: When they persecute you in one town, flee to the next. Truly I tell you, you will not reach all the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.

units.leftText: “A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his lord.
units.rightText: A disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master.

units.leftText: It is enough for the disciple that he be like his teacher, and the servant like his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household!
units.rightText: It is enough for a disciple to be like his teacher, and a servant like his master. If the head of the house has been called Beelzebul, how much more the members of his household!
leftNotes: 10:25 Literally, Lord of the Flies, or the devil
rightNotes: 10:25 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be afraid of them, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not be known.
units.rightText: So do not be afraid of them. For there is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

units.leftText: What I tell you in the darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear whispered in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
units.rightText: What I tell you in the dark, speak in the daylight; what is whispered in your ear, proclaim from the housetops.

units.leftText: Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul. Rather, fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
units.rightText: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Instead, fear the One who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
rightNotes: 10:28 Greek Gehenna

units.leftText: “Aren’t two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls to the ground apart from your Father’s will.
units.rightText: Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground apart from the will of your Father.

units.leftText: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
units.rightText: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

units.leftText: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
units.rightText: So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

units.leftText: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: Therefore everyone who confesses Me before men, I will also confess him before My Father in heaven.

units.leftText: But whoever denies me before men, I will also deny him before my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: But whoever denies Me before men, I will also deny him before My Father in heaven.

units.leftText: For I came to set a man at odds against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
units.rightText: For I have come to turn

units.rightText: A man’s enemies will be the members

units.rightText: Anyone who loves his father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me; anyone who loves his son or daughter more than Me is not worthy of Me;

units.leftText: He who doesn’t take his cross and follow after me isn’t worthy of me.
units.rightText: and anyone who does not take up his cross and follow Me is not worthy of Me.

units.leftText: He who seeks his life will lose it; and he who loses his life for my sake will find it.
units.rightText: Whoever finds his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for My sake will find it.

units.leftText: “He who receives you receives me, and he who receives me receives him who sent me.
units.rightText: He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me.

units.leftText: He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. He who receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.
units.rightText: Whoever receives a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and whoever receives a righteous man because he is a righteous man will receive a righteous man’s reward.

units.leftText: Whoever gives one of these little ones just a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, most certainly I tell you, he will in no way lose his reward.”
units.rightText: And if anyone gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones because he is My disciple, truly I tell you, he will never lose his reward.”

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished directing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and preach in their cities.
units.rightText: After Jesus had finished instructing His twelve disciples, He went on from there to teach and preach in their cities.

units.rightText: Otherwise, what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? Look, those who wear fine clothing are found in kings’ palaces.

units.leftText: For this is he, of whom it is written, ‘Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.’
units.rightText: This is the one about whom it is written:

units.rightText: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is vindicated by her actions.”

units.rightText: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

units.leftText: But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
units.rightText: But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

units.rightText: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.

units.leftText: But I tell you that it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment, than for you.”
units.rightText: But I tell you that it will be more bearable for Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”

units.leftText: At that time, Jesus answered, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.
units.rightText: At that time Jesus declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.

units.leftText: Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.
units.rightText: Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

units.rightText: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.

units.leftText: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
units.rightText: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

units.leftText: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
units.rightText: Take My yoke upon you and learn from Me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.

units.leftText: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
units.rightText: For My yoke is easy and My burden is light.”

units.leftText: But the Pharisees, when they saw it, said to him, “Behold, your disciples do what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”

units.leftText: But he said to them, “Haven’t you read what David did when he was hungry, and those who were with him:
units.rightText: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

units.leftText: how he entered into God’s house and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, nor for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
units.rightText: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.

units.leftText: Or have you not read in the law that on the Sabbath day the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
units.rightText: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?

units.leftText: But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.
units.rightText: But I tell you that One greater than the temple is here.

units.leftText: But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy, and not sacrifice,’ you wouldn’t have condemned the guiltless.
units.rightText: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.
rightNotes: 12:7 Hosea 6:6|HOS 6:6*

units.leftText: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”
units.rightText: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

units.leftText: He departed from there and went into their synagogue.
units.rightText: Moving on from there, Jesus entered their synagogue,

units.leftText: And behold, there was a man with a withered hand. They asked him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day?” so that they might accuse him.
units.rightText: and a man with a withered hand was there. In order to accuse Jesus, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

units.leftText: He said to them, “What man is there among you who has one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, won’t he grab on to it and lift it out?
units.rightText: He replied, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?

units.leftText: Of how much more value then is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.”
units.rightText: How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”

units.leftText: Then he told the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out; and it was restored whole, just like the other.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored to full use, just like the other.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees went out and conspired against him, how they might destroy him.
units.rightText: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus.

units.leftText: Jesus, perceiving that, withdrew from there. Great multitudes followed him; and he healed them all,
units.rightText: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them all,

units.leftText: and commanded them that they should not make him known,
units.rightText: warning them not to make Him known.

units.leftText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,

units.leftText: “Behold, my servant whom I have chosen,
units.rightText: “Here is My Servant,

units.leftText: He will not strive, nor shout,
units.rightText: He will not quarrel or cry out;

units.leftText: He won’t break a bruised reed.

units.leftText: Then one possessed by a demon, blind and mute, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that the blind and mute man both spoke and saw.
units.rightText: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed the man so that he could speak and see.

units.leftText: All the multitudes were amazed, and said, “Can this be the son of David?”
units.rightText: The crowds were astounded and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”

units.leftText: But when the Pharisees heard it, they said, “This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
units.rightText: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.”
rightNotes: 12:24 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub; also in verse 27

units.leftText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.
units.rightText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.

units.leftText: If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?
units.rightText: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?

units.leftText: If I by Beelzebul cast out demons, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
units.rightText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

units.leftText: But if I by the Spirit of God cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come upon you.
units.rightText: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

units.leftText: Or how can one enter into the house of the strong man and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.
units.rightText: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.

units.leftText: “He who is not with me is against me, and he who doesn’t gather with me, scatters.
units.rightText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.

units.leftText: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven men.
units.rightText: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

units.leftText: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this age, or in that which is to come.
units.rightText: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.

units.leftText: “Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree corrupt and its fruit corrupt; for the tree is known by its fruit.
units.rightText: Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad, for a tree is known by its fruit.

units.leftText: You offspring of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks.
units.rightText: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks.

units.leftText: The good man out of his good treasure brings out good things, and the evil man out of his evil treasure brings out evil things.
units.rightText: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.

units.leftText: I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment.
units.rightText: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.

units.leftText: For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”
units.rightText: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.”

units.leftText: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
units.rightText: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.”

units.leftText: But he answered them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, but no sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
units.rightText: Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

units.leftText: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
units.rightText: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

units.leftText: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, someone greater than Jonah is here.
units.rightText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

units.leftText: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, someone greater than Solomon is here.
units.rightText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

units.leftText: “When an unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he passes through waterless places seeking rest, and doesn’t find it.
units.rightText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.

units.leftText: Then he says, ‘I will return into my house from which I came;’ and when he has come back, he finds it empty, swept, and put in order.
units.rightText: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ On its return, it finds the house vacant, swept clean, and put in order.

units.leftText: Then he goes and takes with himself seven other spirits more evil than he is, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first. Even so will it be also to this evil generation.”
units.rightText: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first. So will it be with this wicked generation.”

units.leftText: While he was yet speaking to the multitudes, behold, his mother and his brothers stood outside, seeking to speak to him.
units.rightText: While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, His mother and brothers stood outside, wanting to speak to Him.

units.leftText: One said to him, “Behold, your mother and your brothers stand outside, seeking to speak to you.”
units.rightText: Someone told Him, “Look, Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak to You.”
rightNotes: 12:47 WH does not include verse 47.

units.leftText: But he answered him who spoke to him, “Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?”
units.rightText: But Jesus replied, “Who is My mother, and who are My brothers?”

units.leftText: He stretched out his hand toward his disciples, and said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
units.rightText: Pointing to His disciples, He said, “Here are My mother and My brothers.

units.leftText: For whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.”
units.rightText: For whoever does the will of My Father in heaven is My brother and sister and mother.”

units.leftText: On that day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the seaside.
units.rightText: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the sea.

units.leftText: Great multitudes gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat and sat; and all the multitude stood on the beach.
units.rightText: Such large crowds gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore.

units.leftText: He spoke to them many things in parables, saying, “Behold, a farmer went out to sow.
units.rightText: And He told them many things in parables, saying, “A farmer went out to sow his seed.

units.leftText: As he sowed, some seeds fell by the roadside, and the birds came and devoured them.
units.rightText: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.

units.leftText: Others fell on rocky ground, where they didn’t have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of earth.
units.rightText: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.

units.leftText: When the sun had risen, they were scorched. Because they had no root, they withered away.
units.rightText: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.

units.leftText: Others fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked them.
units.rightText: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.

units.leftText: Others fell on good soil and yielded fruit: some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.
units.rightText: Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop — a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.

units.leftText: He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: He who has ears, let him hear.”
rightNotes: 13:9 BYZ and TR ears to hear; also in verse 43

units.leftText: The disciples came, and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
units.rightText: Then the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why do You speak to the people in parables?”

units.leftText: He answered them, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but it is not given to them.
units.rightText: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.

units.leftText: For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever doesn’t have, from him will be taken away even that which he has.
units.rightText: Whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

units.leftText: Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they don’t see, and hearing, they don’t hear, neither do they understand.
units.rightText: This is why I speak to them in parables:

units.leftText: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says,
units.rightText: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled:

units.leftText: for this people’s heart has grown callous,
units.rightText: For this people’s heart has grown callous;

units.leftText: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.
units.rightText: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.

units.leftText: For most certainly I tell you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them; and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.
units.rightText: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.

units.leftText: “Hear, then, the parable of the farmer.
units.rightText: Consider, then, the parable of the sower:

units.leftText: When anyone hears the word of the Kingdom and doesn’t understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away that which has been sown in his heart. This is what was sown by the roadside.
units.rightText: When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.
rightNotes: 13:19 Literally the one sown; also in verses 20, 22, and 23

units.leftText: What was sown on the rocky places, this is he who hears the word and immediately with joy receives it;
units.rightText: The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.

units.leftText: yet he has no root in himself, but endures for a while. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
units.rightText: But since he has no root, he remains for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.

units.leftText: What was sown among the thorns, this is he who hears the word, but the cares of this age and the deceitfulness of riches choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
units.rightText: The seed sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

units.leftText: What was sown on the good ground, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some one hundred times as much, some sixty, and some thirty.”
units.rightText: But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and produces a crop — a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.”

units.leftText: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field,
units.rightText: Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.

units.leftText: but while people slept, his enemy came and sowed darnel weeds also among the wheat, and went away.
units.rightText: But while everyone was asleep, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.
leftNotes: 13:25 darnel is a weed grass (probably bearded darnel or lolium temulentum) that looks very much like wheat until it is mature, when the difference becomes very apparent.

units.leftText: But when the blade sprang up and produced grain, then the darnel weeds appeared also.
units.rightText: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.

units.leftText: The servants of the householder came and said to him, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where did these darnel weeds come from?’
units.rightText: The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’

units.leftText: “He said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’
units.rightText: ‘An enemy did this,’ he replied.

units.leftText: “But he said, ‘No, lest perhaps while you gather up the darnel weeds, you root up the wheat with them.
units.rightText: ‘No,’ he said, ‘if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.

units.leftText: Let both grow together until the harvest, and in the harvest time I will tell the reapers, “First, gather up the darnel weeds, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.”’”
units.rightText: Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the harvesters: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.’”

units.leftText: He set another parable before them, saying, “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took, and sowed in his field,
units.rightText: He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his field.

units.leftText: which indeed is smaller than all seeds. But when it is grown, it is greater than the herbs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.”
units.rightText: Although it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.”

units.leftText: He spoke another parable to them. “The Kingdom of Heaven is like yeast which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, until it was all leavened.”
units.rightText: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
leftNotes: 13:33 literally, three sata. Three sata is about 39 liters or a bit more than a bushel

units.leftText: Jesus spoke all these things in parables to the multitudes; and without a parable, he didn’t speak to them,
units.rightText: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.

units.leftText: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
units.rightText: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet:

units.leftText: Then Jesus sent the multitudes away, and went into the house. His disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the darnel weeds of the field.”
units.rightText: Then Jesus dismissed the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”

units.leftText: He answered them, “He who sows the good seed is the Son of Man,
units.rightText: He replied, “The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.

units.leftText: the field is the world, the good seeds are the children of the Kingdom, and the darnel weeds are the children of the evil one.
units.rightText: The field is the world, and the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one,

units.leftText: The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
units.rightText: and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.

units.leftText: As therefore the darnel weeds are gathered up and burned with fire; so will it be at the end of this age.
units.rightText: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.

units.leftText: The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather out of his Kingdom all things that cause stumbling and those who do iniquity,
units.rightText: The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will weed out of His kingdom every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness.

units.leftText: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
units.rightText: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the Kingdom of their Father. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.
units.rightText: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.
rightNotes: 13:43 See Daniel 12:3|DAN 12:3*.

units.leftText: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid. In his joy, he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
units.rightText: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.

units.leftText: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a merchant seeking fine pearls,
units.rightText: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.

units.leftText: who having found one pearl of great price, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.
units.rightText: When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it.

units.leftText: “Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a dragnet that was cast into the sea and gathered some fish of every kind,
units.rightText: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish.

units.leftText: which, when it was filled, fishermen drew up on the beach. They sat down and gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw away.
units.rightText: When it was full, the men pulled it ashore. Then they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away.

units.leftText: So it will be in the end of the world. The angels will come and separate the wicked from among the righteous,
units.rightText: So will it be at the end of the age: The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous

units.leftText: and will cast them into the furnace of fire. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
units.rightText: and throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Have you understood all these things?”
units.rightText: Have you understood all these things?”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”
units.rightText: Then He told them, “For this reason, every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.”

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished these parables, he departed from there.
units.rightText: When Jesus had finished these parables, He withdrew from that place.

units.leftText: Coming into his own country, he taught them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
units.rightText: Coming to His hometown, He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were astonished. “Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?” they asked.

units.leftText: Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother called Mary, and his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?
units.rightText: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
rightNotes: 13:55 BYZ and TR Joses; see Mark 6:3|MRK 6:3*.

units.leftText: Aren’t all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of these things?”
units.rightText: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”

units.leftText: They were offended by him.
units.rightText: And they took offense at Him.

units.leftText: He didn’t do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.
units.rightText: And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief.

units.leftText: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the report concerning Jesus,
units.rightText: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus

units.leftText: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead. That is why these powers work in him.”
units.rightText: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”

units.leftText: For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
units.rightText: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife,

units.leftText: For John said to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
units.rightText: because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”

units.rightText: Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet.

units.leftText: But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced among them and pleased Herod.
units.rightText: On Herod’s birthday, however, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod

units.leftText: Therefore he promised with an oath to give her whatever she should ask.
units.rightText: so much that he promised with an oath to give to her whatever she asked.

units.leftText: She, being prompted by her mother, said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptizer.”
units.rightText: Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”

units.leftText: The king was grieved, but for the sake of his oaths and of those who sat at the table with him, he commanded it to be given,
units.rightText: The king was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted

units.leftText: and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
units.rightText: and sent to have John beheaded in the prison.

units.leftText: His head was brought on a platter and given to the young lady; and she brought it to her mother.
units.rightText: John’s head was brought in on a platter and presented to the girl, who carried it to her mother.

units.leftText: His disciples came, took the body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
units.rightText: Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. And they went and informed Jesus.

units.leftText: Now when Jesus heard this, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place apart. When the multitudes heard it, they followed him on foot from the cities.
units.rightText: When Jesus heard about John, He withdrew by boat privately to a solitary place. But the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns.

units.leftText: Jesus went out, and he saw a great multitude. He had compassion on them and healed their sick.
units.rightText: When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them and healed their sick.

units.leftText: When evening had come, his disciples came to him, saying, “This place is deserted, and the hour is already late. Send the multitudes away, that they may go into the villages, and buy themselves food.”
units.rightText: When evening came, the disciples came to Him and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late. Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.”

units.leftText: But Jesus said to them, “They don’t need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
units.rightText: “They do not need to go away,” Jesus replied. “You give them something to eat.”

units.leftText: They told him, “We only have here five loaves and two fish.”
units.rightText: “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered.

units.leftText: He said, “Bring them here to me.”
units.rightText: “Bring them here to Me,” Jesus said.

units.rightText: Aware of their conversation, Jesus said, “You of little faith, why are you debating among yourselves about having no bread?

units.leftText: Don’t you yet perceive or remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you took up,

units.rightText: How do you not understand that I was not telling you about bread? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”

units.rightText: Then they understood that He was not telling them to beware of the leaven used in bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

units.rightText: Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
