units.leftText: but whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a huge millstone were hung around his neck and that he were sunk in the depths of the sea.
units.rightText: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.

units.leftText: “Woe to the world because of occasions of stumbling! For it must be that the occasions come, but woe to that person through whom the occasion comes!
units.rightText: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!

units.leftText: If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life maimed or crippled, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the eternal fire.
units.rightText: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.

units.leftText: If your eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from you. It is better for you to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the Gehenna of fire.
units.rightText: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
rightNotes: 18:9 Or the hell of fire; Greek the Gehenna of fire

units.leftText: See that you don’t despise one of these little ones, for I tell you that in heaven their angels always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
rightNotes: 18:10 BYZ and TR include 11*For the Son of Man came to save the lost; see Luke 19:10|LUK 19:10*.

units.leftText: For the Son of Man came to save that which was lost.
“What do you think? If a man has one hundred sheep, and one of them goes astray, doesn’t he leave the ninety-nine, go to the mountains, and seek that which has gone astray?
units.rightText: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?

units.leftText: If he finds it, most certainly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine which have not gone astray.
units.rightText: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.

units.leftText: Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
units.rightText: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.

units.leftText: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
units.rightText: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
rightNotes: 18:15 NE and WH do not include against you.

units.leftText: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
units.rightText: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
rightNotes: 18:16 Deuteronomy 19:15|DEU 19:15*

units.leftText: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.
units.rightText: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, whatever things you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever things you release on earth will have been released in heaven.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.

units.leftText: Again, assuredly I tell you, that if two of you will agree on earth concerning anything that they will ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in heaven.
units.rightText: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.

units.leftText: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
units.rightText: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”

units.leftText: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”
units.rightText: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
rightNotes: 18:22 Or seventy times seven; see Genesis 4:24|GEN 4:24* LXX

units.leftText: Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
units.rightText: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

units.leftText: When he had begun to settle, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
units.rightText: As he began the settlements, a debtor owing ten thousand talents was brought to him.
leftNotes: 18:24 Ten thousand talents (about 300 metric tons of silver) represents an extremely large sum of money, equivalent to about 60,000,000 denarii, where one denarius was typical of one day’s wages for agricultural labor.
rightNotes: 18:24 A talent was worth about twenty years’ wages for a laborer.

units.leftText: But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
units.rightText: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.

units.leftText: The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’
units.rightText: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’

units.leftText: The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the debt.
units.rightText: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.

units.leftText: “But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
units.rightText: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
leftNotes: 18:28 100 denarii was about one sixtieth of a talent, or about 500 grams (1.1 pounds) of silver.
rightNotes: 18:28 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’
units.rightText: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’

units.leftText: He would not, but went and cast him into prison until he should pay back that which was due.
units.rightText: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.

units.leftText: So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.
units.rightText: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.

units.leftText: Then his lord called him in and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.
units.rightText: Then the master summoned him and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.

units.leftText: Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’
units.rightText: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’

units.leftText: His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors until he should pay all that was due to him.
units.rightText: In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.

units.leftText: So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”
units.rightText: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished these words, he departed from Galilee and came into the borders of Judea beyond the Jordan.
units.rightText: When Jesus had finished saying these things, He left Galilee and went into the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

units.leftText: Great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.
units.rightText: Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them there.

units.leftText: Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”
units.rightText: Then some Pharisees came and tested Him by asking, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?”

units.leftText: He answered, “Haven’t you read that he who made them from the beginning made them male and female,
units.rightText: Jesus answered, “Have you not read that from the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’
rightNotes: 19:4 Genesis 1:27|GEN 1:27*; Genesis 5:2

units.leftText: and said, ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined to his wife; and the two shall become one flesh’?
units.rightText: and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’ ?
rightNotes: 19:5 Genesis 2:24|GEN 2:24* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: So that they are no more two, but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, don’t let man tear apart.”
units.rightText: So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate.”

units.leftText: They asked him, “Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of divorce and divorce her?”
units.rightText: “Why then,” they asked, “did Moses order a man to give his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away? ”
rightNotes: 19:7 See Deuteronomy 24:1|DEU 24:1*.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Moses, because of the hardness of your hearts, allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
units.rightText: Jesus replied, “Moses permitted you to divorce your wives because of your hardness of heart. But it was not this way from the beginning.

units.leftText: I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another, commits adultery; and he who marries her when she is divorced commits adultery.”
units.rightText: Now I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery. ”
rightNotes: 19:9 SBL and BYZ include And he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery; see Matthew 5:32|MAT 5:32*.

units.leftText: His disciples said to him, “If this is the case of the man with his wife, it is not expedient to marry.”
units.rightText: His disciples said to Him, “If this is the case between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”

units.leftText: But he said to them, “Not all men can receive this saying, but those to whom it is given.
units.rightText: “Not everyone can accept this word,” He replied, “but only those to whom it has been given.

units.leftText: For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men; and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven’s sake. He who is able to receive it, let him receive it.”
units.rightText: For there are eunuchs who were born that way; others were made that way by men; and still others live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.”

units.leftText: Then little children were brought to him that he should lay his hands on them and pray; and the disciples rebuked them.
units.rightText: Then little children were brought to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them and pray for them. And the disciples rebuked those who brought them.

units.leftText: But Jesus said, “Allow the little children, and don’t forbid them to come to me; for the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to ones like these.”
units.rightText: But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these.”

units.leftText: He laid his hands on them, and departed from there.
units.rightText: And after He had placed His hands on them, He went on from there.

units.leftText: Behold, one came to him and said, “Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?”
units.rightText: Just then a man came up to Jesus and inquired, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?”

units.leftText: He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, that is, God. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
units.rightText: “Why do you ask Me about what is good?” Jesus replied. “There is only One who is good. If you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
leftNotes: 19:17 So MT and TR. NU reads “Why do you ask me about what is good?”
rightNotes: 19:17 BYZ and TR 16*...“Good Teacher, what good thing must I do to obtain eternal life?” 17*“Why do you call Me good?”See Mark 10:17–18|MRK 10:17-18* and Luke 18:18–19.

units.leftText: He said to him, “Which ones?”
units.rightText: “Which ones?” the man asked.

units.leftText: ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ And, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
units.rightText: honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
rightNotes: 19:19 Exodus 20:12–16|EXO 20:12-16*; Leviticus 19:18; Deuteronomy 5:16–20

units.leftText: The young man said to him, “All these things I have observed from my youth. What do I still lack?”
units.rightText: “All these I have kept,” said the young man. “What do I still lack?”

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have, and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
units.rightText: Jesus told him, “If you want to be perfect, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

units.leftText: But when the young man heard this, he went away sad, for he was one who had great possessions.
units.rightText: When the young man heard this, he went away in sorrow, because he had great wealth.

units.leftText: Jesus said to his disciples, “Most certainly I say to you, a rich man will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven with difficulty.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.

units.leftText: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom.”
units.rightText: Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

units.leftText: When the disciples heard it, they were exceedingly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
units.rightText: When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and asked, “Who then can be saved?”

units.leftText: Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
units.rightText: Jesus looked at them and said, “With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”

units.leftText: Then Peter answered, “Behold, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?”
units.rightText: “Look,” Peter replied, “we have left everything to follow You. What then will there be for us?”

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly I tell you that you who have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Man will sit on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
units.rightText: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, in the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on His glorious throne, you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
rightNotes: 19:28 Or in the regeneration

units.leftText: Everyone who has left houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, will receive one hundred times, and will inherit eternal life.
units.rightText: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for the sake of My name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.
rightNotes: 19:29 NE, WH, and NA do not include or wife.

units.leftText: But many will be last who are first, and first who are last.
units.rightText: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.[’’]

units.leftText: “For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who was the master of a household, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard.
units.rightText: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.

units.leftText: When he had agreed with the laborers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
units.rightText: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
leftNotes: 20:2 A denarius is a silver Roman coin worth 1/25th of a Roman aureus. This was a common wage for a day of farm labor.
rightNotes: 20:2 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; similarly in verses 9, 10, and 13.

units.leftText: He went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
units.rightText: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.
leftNotes: 20:3 Time was measured from sunrise to sunset, so the third hour would be about 9:00 a.m.
rightNotes: 20:3 That is, about nine in the morning

units.leftText: He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’ So they went their way.
units.rightText: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’

units.leftText: Again he went out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did likewise.
units.rightText: So they went.

units.leftText: About the eleventh hour he went out and found others standing idle. He said to them, ‘Why do you stand here all day idle?’
units.rightText: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.
rightNotes: 20:6 That is, about five in the afternoon; also in verse 9

units.leftText: “They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’
units.rightText: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered.

units.leftText: “When evening had come, the lord of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the laborers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last to the first.’
units.rightText: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’

units.leftText: “When those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, they each received a denarius.
units.rightText: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.

units.leftText: When the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they likewise each received a denarius.
units.rightText: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.

units.leftText: When they received it, they murmured against the master of the household,
units.rightText: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.

units.leftText: saying, ‘These last have spent one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat!’
units.rightText: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’

units.leftText: “But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Didn’t you agree with me for a denarius?
units.rightText: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?

units.leftText: Take that which is yours, and go your way. It is my desire to give to this last just as much as to you.
units.rightText: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.

units.leftText: Isn’t it lawful for me to do what I want to with what I own? Or is your eye evil, because I am good?’
units.rightText: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’

units.leftText: So the last will be first, and the first last. For many are called, but few are chosen.”
units.rightText: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”
rightNotes: 20:16 BYZ and TR include For many are called, but few are chosen.

units.leftText: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,
units.rightText: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said,

units.leftText: “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
units.rightText: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death

units.leftText: and will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock, to scourge, and to crucify; and the third day he will be raised up.”
units.rightText: and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.”

units.leftText: Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, kneeling and asking a certain thing of him.
units.rightText: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.

units.leftText: He said to her, “What do you want?”
units.rightText: “What do you want?” He inquired.

units.leftText: But Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?”
units.rightText: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?”
rightNotes: 20:22 BYZ includes or be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized. TR is similar.

units.leftText: He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with; but to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give, but it is for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
units.rightText: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”
rightNotes: 20:23 BYZ and TR include and be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized.

units.leftText: When the ten heard it, they were indignant with the two brothers.
units.rightText: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.

units.leftText: But Jesus summoned them, and said, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
units.rightText: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.

units.leftText: It shall not be so among you; but whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant.
units.rightText: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant,
leftNotes: 20:26 TR reads “let him be” instead of “shall be”

units.leftText: Whoever desires to be first among you shall be your bondservant,
units.rightText: and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave —

units.leftText: even as the Son of Man came not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
units.rightText: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”

units.leftText: As they went out from Jericho, a great multitude followed him.
units.rightText: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.

units.leftText: Behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
units.rightText: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

units.leftText: The multitude rebuked them, telling them that they should be quiet, but they cried out even more, “Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!”
units.rightText: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”

units.leftText: Jesus stood still and called them, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
units.rightText: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.

units.leftText: They told him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”
units.rightText: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”

units.leftText: Jesus, being moved with compassion, touched their eyes; and immediately their eyes received their sight, and they followed him.
units.rightText: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.

units.leftText: When they came near to Jerusalem and came to Bethsphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
units.rightText: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples,

units.leftText: saying to them, “Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
units.rightText: saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.

units.leftText: If anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord needs them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
units.rightText: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”

units.leftText: All this was done that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
units.rightText: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet:

units.leftText: “Tell the daughter of Zion,
units.rightText: “Say to the Daughter of Zion,

units.leftText: The disciples went and did just as Jesus commanded them,
units.rightText: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.

units.leftText: and brought the donkey and the colt and laid their clothes on them; and he sat on them.
units.rightText: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.

units.leftText: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
units.rightText: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.

units.leftText: The multitudes who went in front of him, and those who followed, kept shouting, “Hosanna to the son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
units.rightText: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting:
leftNotes: 21:9 “Hosanna” means “save us” or “help us, we pray”.

units.leftText: When he had come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”
units.rightText: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”

units.leftText: The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”
units.rightText: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”

units.leftText: Jesus entered into the temple of God and drove out all of those who sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the money changers’ tables and the seats of those who sold the doves.
units.rightText: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
rightNotes: 21:12 Literally the temple; also in verses 15 and 23; BYZ and TR the temple of God

units.leftText: He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers!”
units.rightText: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’ ”
rightNotes: 21:13 Jeremiah 7:11|JER 7:11*

units.leftText: The lame and the blind came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
units.rightText: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.

units.leftText: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children who were crying in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the son of David!” they were indignant,
units.rightText: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”

units.leftText: and said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?”
units.rightText: “Do You hear what these children are saying?” they asked.

units.leftText: He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, and camped there.
units.rightText: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night.

units.leftText: Now in the morning, as he returned to the city, he was hungry.
units.rightText: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.

units.leftText: Seeing a fig tree by the road, he came to it and found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, “Let there be no fruit from you forever!”
units.rightText: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.

units.leftText: When the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree immediately wither away?”
units.rightText: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you told this mountain, ‘Be taken up and cast into the sea,’ it would be done.
units.rightText: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.

units.leftText: All things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”
units.rightText: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”

units.leftText: When he had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, “By what authority do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?”
units.rightText: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “I also will ask you one question, which if you tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
units.rightText: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.

units.leftText: The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?”
units.rightText: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?”

units.leftText: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the multitude, for all hold John as a prophet.”
units.rightText: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”

units.rightText: So they answered, “We do not know.”

units.leftText: But what do you think? A man had two sons, and he came to the first, and said, ‘Son, go work today in my vineyard.’
units.rightText: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’

units.leftText: He answered, ‘I will not,’ but afterward he changed his mind, and went.

units.leftText: Which of the two did the will of his father?”
units.rightText: Which of the two did the will of his father?”

units.leftText: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you didn’t believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. When you saw it, you didn’t even repent afterward, that you might believe him.
units.rightText: For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.

units.leftText: “Hear another parable. There was a man who was a master of a household who planted a vineyard, set a hedge about it, dug a wine press in it, built a tower, leased it out to farmers, and went into another country.
units.rightText: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.

units.leftText: When the season for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the farmers to receive his fruit.
units.rightText: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.

units.leftText: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
units.rightText: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.

units.leftText: Again, he sent other servants more than the first; and they treated them the same way.
units.rightText: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.

units.leftText: But afterward he sent to them his son, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
units.rightText: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.

units.leftText: But the farmers, when they saw the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let’s kill him and seize his inheritance.’
units.rightText: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’

units.leftText: So they took him and threw him out of the vineyard, then killed him.
units.rightText: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.

units.leftText: When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
units.rightText: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”

units.leftText: They told him, “He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will lease out the vineyard to other farmers who will give him the fruit in its season.”
units.rightText: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”

units.leftText: Jesus said to them, “Did you never read in the Scriptures,
units.rightText: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures:

units.leftText: “Therefore I tell you, God’s Kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a nation producing its fruit.
units.rightText: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.

units.leftText: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but on whomever it will fall, it will scatter him as dust.”
units.rightText: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed. ”
