units.leftText: When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spoke about them.
units.rightText: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.

units.leftText: When they sought to seize him, they feared the multitudes, because they considered him to be a prophet.
units.rightText: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.

units.leftText: Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying,
units.rightText: Once again, Jesus spoke to them in parables:

units.leftText: “The Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who made a wedding feast for his son,
units.rightText: “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding banquet for his son.

units.leftText: and sent out his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding feast, but they would not come.
units.rightText: He sent his servants to call those he had invited to the banquet, but they refused to come.

units.leftText: Again he sent out other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who are invited, “Behold, I have prepared my dinner. My cattle and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast!”’
units.rightText: Again, he sent other servants and said, ‘Tell those who have been invited that I have prepared my dinner. My oxen and fattened cattle have been killed, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding banquet.’

units.leftText: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his own farm, another to his merchandise;
units.rightText: But they paid no attention and went away, one to his field, another to his business.

units.leftText: and the rest grabbed his servants, treated them shamefully, and killed them.
units.rightText: The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.

units.leftText: When the king heard that, he was angry, and sent his armies, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
units.rightText: The king was enraged, and he sent his troops to destroy those murderers and burn their city.

units.leftText: “Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding is ready, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.
units.rightText: Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding banquet is ready, but those I invited were not worthy.

units.leftText: Go therefore to the intersections of the highways, and as many as you may find, invite to the wedding feast.’
units.rightText: Go therefore to the crossroads and invite to the banquet as many as you can find.’

units.leftText: Those servants went out into the highways and gathered together as many as they found, both bad and good. The wedding was filled with guests.
units.rightText: So the servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they could find, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.

units.leftText: “But when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who didn’t have on wedding clothing,
units.rightText: But when the king came in to see the guests, he spotted a man who was not dressed in wedding clothes.

units.leftText: and he said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not wearing wedding clothing?’ He was speechless.
units.rightText: ‘Friend,’ he asked, ‘how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’

units.leftText: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Bind him hand and foot, take him away, and throw him into the outer darkness. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.’
units.rightText: Then the king told the servants, ‘Tie him hand and foot, and throw him into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

units.leftText: For many are called, but few chosen.”
units.rightText: For many are called, but few are chosen.”

units.leftText: Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might entrap him in his talk.
units.rightText: Then the Pharisees went out and conspired to trap Jesus in His words.

units.leftText: They sent their disciples to him, along with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are honest, and teach the way of God in truth, no matter whom you teach; for you aren’t partial to anyone.
units.rightText: They sent their disciples to Him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and that You teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You seek favor from no one, because You pay no attention to external appearance.

units.leftText: Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
units.rightText: So tell us what You think: Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”

units.leftText: But Jesus perceived their wickedness, and said, “Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
units.rightText: But Jesus knew their evil intent and said, “You hypocrites, why are you testing Me?

units.leftText: Show me the tax money.”
units.rightText: Show Me the coin used for the tax.”

units.leftText: He asked them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
units.rightText: “Whose image is this,” He asked, “and whose inscription?”

units.leftText: They said to him, “Caesar’s.”
units.rightText: “Caesar’s,” they answered.

units.leftText: When they heard it, they marveled, and left him and went away.
units.rightText: And when they heard this, they were amazed. So they left Him and went away.

units.leftText: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,
units.rightText: That same day the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him.

units.leftText: saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
units.rightText: “Teacher,” they said, “Moses declared that if a man dies without having children, his brother is to marry the widow and raise up offspring for him.
rightNotes: 22:24 Deuteronomy 25:5|DEU 25:5*

units.leftText: Now there were with us seven brothers. The first married and died, and having no offspring left his wife to his brother.
units.rightText: Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married and died without having children. So he left his wife to his brother.

units.leftText: In the same way, the second also, and the third, to the seventh.
units.rightText: The same thing happened to the second and third brothers, down to the seventh.

units.leftText: After them all, the woman died.
units.rightText: And last of all, the woman died.

units.leftText: In the resurrection therefore, whose wife will she be of the seven? For they all had her.”
units.rightText: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be of the seven? For all of them were married to her.”

units.leftText: But Jesus answered them, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.

units.leftText: For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like God’s angels in heaven.
units.rightText: In the resurrection, people will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
rightNotes: 22:30 SBL, BYZ, and TR the angels of God

units.leftText: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read that which was spoken to you by God, saying,
units.rightText: But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:

units.leftText: ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
units.rightText: ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’ ? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
rightNotes: 22:32 Exodus 3:6|EXO 3:6*

units.leftText: When the multitudes heard it, they were astonished at his teaching.
units.rightText: When the crowds heard this, they were astonished at His teaching.

units.leftText: But the Pharisees, when they heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered themselves together.
units.rightText: And when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they themselves gathered together.

units.leftText: One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, testing him.
units.rightText: One of them, an expert in the law, tested Him with a question:

units.leftText: “Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the law?”
units.rightText: “Teacher, which commandment is the greatest in the Law?”

units.leftText: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’
units.rightText: Jesus declared, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’
rightNotes: 22:37 Deuteronomy 6:5|DEU 6:5*

units.leftText: This is the first and great commandment.
units.rightText: This is the first and greatest commandment.

units.leftText: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
units.rightText: And the second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’
rightNotes: 22:39 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”
units.rightText: All the Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”

units.leftText: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus asked them a question,
units.rightText: While the Pharisees were assembled, Jesus questioned them:

units.leftText: saying, “What do you think of the Christ? Whose son is he?”
units.rightText: “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is He?”

units.leftText: He said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
units.rightText: Jesus said to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call Him ‘Lord’? For he says:

units.leftText: ‘The Lord said to my Lord,
units.rightText: ‘The Lord said to my Lord,

units.leftText: “If then David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
units.rightText: So if David calls Him ‘Lord,’ how can He be David’s son?”

units.leftText: No one was able to answer him a word, neither did any man dare ask him any more questions from that day forward.
units.rightText: No one was able to answer a word, and from that day on no one dared to question Him any further.

units.leftText: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes and to his disciples,
units.rightText: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to His disciples:

units.leftText: saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
units.rightText: “The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat.

units.leftText: All things therefore whatever they tell you to observe, observe and do, but don’t do their works; for they say, and don’t do.
units.rightText: So practice and observe everything they tell you. But do not do what they do, for they do not practice what they preach.

units.leftText: For they bind heavy burdens that are grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to help them.
units.rightText: They tie up heavy, burdensome loads and lay them on men’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them.
rightNotes: 23:4 SBL, NE, and WH They tie up heavy loads

units.leftText: But they do all their works to be seen by men. They make their phylacteries broad and enlarge the fringes of their garments,
units.rightText: All their deeds are done for men to see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels.
leftNotes: 23:5 phylacteries (tefillin in Hebrew) are small leather pouches that some Jewish men wear on their forehead and arm in prayer. They are used to carry a small scroll with some Scripture in it. See Deuteronomy 6:8.

units.leftText: and love the place of honor at feasts, the best seats in the synagogues,
units.rightText: They love the places of honor at banquets, the chief seats in the synagogues,

units.leftText: the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called ‘Rabbi, Rabbi’ by men.
units.rightText: the greetings in the marketplaces, and the title of ‘Rabbi’ by which they are addressed.
rightNotes: 23:7 Literally and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by men

units.leftText: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi’, for one is your teacher, the Christ, and all of you are brothers.
units.rightText: But you are not to be called ‘Rabbi,’ for you have one Teacher, and you are all brothers.

units.leftText: Call no man on the earth your father, for one is your Father, he who is in heaven.
units.rightText: And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.

units.leftText: Neither be called masters, for one is your master, the Christ.
units.rightText: Nor are you to be called instructors, for you have one Instructor, the Christ.

units.leftText: But he who is greatest among you will be your servant.
units.rightText: The greatest among you shall be your servant.

units.leftText: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
units.rightText: For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you devour widows’ houses, and as a pretense you make long prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You shut the kingdom of heaven in men’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor will you let in those who wish to enter.
rightNotes: 23:13 BYZ and TR include 14*Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. Therefore you will receive greater condemnation.See Mark 12:40|MRK 12:40* and Luke 20:47.

units.leftText: “But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the Kingdom of Heaven against men; for you don’t enter in yourselves, neither do you allow those who are entering in to enter.
leftNotes: 23:14 Some Greek texts reverse the order of verses 13 and 14, and some omit verse 13, numbering verse 14 as 13. NU omits verse 14.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel around by sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of Gehenna as yourselves.
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him twice as much a son of hell as you are.
rightNotes: 23:15 Greek Gehenna; also in verse 33

units.leftText: “Woe to you, you blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the temple, he is obligated.’
units.rightText: Woe to you, blind guides! You say, ‘If anyone swears by the temple, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the temple, he is bound by his oath.’

units.leftText: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold?
units.rightText: You blind fools! Which is greater: the gold, or the temple that makes it sacred?

units.leftText: And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it, he is obligated.’
units.rightText: And you say, ‘If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gift on it, he is bound by his oath.’

units.leftText: You blind fools! For which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?
units.rightText: You blind men! Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?

units.leftText: He therefore who swears by the altar, swears by it and by everything on it.
units.rightText: So then, he who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

units.leftText: He who swears by the temple, swears by it and by him who has been living in it.
units.rightText: And he who swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it.

units.leftText: He who swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God and by him who sits on it.
units.rightText: And he who swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the One who sits on it.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have left undone the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. But you ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin. But you have disregarded the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness. You should have practiced the latter, without neglecting the former.
leftNotes: 23:23 cumin is an aromatic seed from Cuminum cyminum, resembling caraway in flavor and appearance. It is used as a spice.

units.leftText: You blind guides, who strain out a gnat, and swallow a camel!
units.rightText: You blind guides! You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.
rightNotes: 23:24 See Leviticus 11:4|LEV 11:4* and Leviticus 11:23, where camels and gnats are both forbidden as food.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and unrighteousness.
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside they are full of greed and self-indulgence.

units.leftText: You blind Pharisee, first clean the inside of the cup and of the platter, that its outside may become clean also.
units.rightText: Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and dish, so that the outside may become clean as well.
rightNotes: 23:26 NA does not include and dish.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitened tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful, but inwardly are full of dead men’s bones and of all uncleanness.
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside but on the inside are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of impurity.

units.leftText: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous to men, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
units.rightText: In the same way, on the outside you appear to be righteous, but on the inside you are full of hypocrisy and wickedness.

units.leftText: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the tombs of the righteous,
units.rightText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous.

units.leftText: and say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we wouldn’t have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.’
units.rightText: And you say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’

units.leftText: Therefore you testify to yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.
units.rightText: So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of those who murdered the prophets.

units.leftText: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers.
units.rightText: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers.
rightNotes: 23:32 Or Go ahead, then, and complete

units.leftText: You serpents, you offspring of vipers, how will you escape the judgment of Gehenna?
units.rightText: You snakes! You brood of vipers! How will you escape the sentence of hell?

units.leftText: Therefore, behold, I send to you prophets, wise men, and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and persecute from city to city,
units.rightText: Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers. Some of them you will kill and crucify, and others you will flog in your synagogues and persecute from town to town.

units.leftText: that on you may come all the righteous blood shed on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zachariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the sanctuary and the altar.
units.rightText: And so upon you will come all the righteous blood shed on earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.

units.leftText: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
units.rightText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

units.leftText: Behold, your house is left to you desolate.
units.rightText: Look, your house is left to you desolate.
rightNotes: 23:38 NE and WH do not include desolate.

units.leftText: For I tell you, you will not see me from now on, until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
units.rightText: For I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”

units.leftText: Jesus went out from the temple, and was going on his way. His disciples came to him to show him the buildings of the temple.
units.rightText: As Jesus left the temple and was walking away, His disciples came up to Him to point out its buildings.

units.leftText: But he answered them, “You see all of these things, don’t you? Most certainly I tell you, there will not be left here one stone on another, that will not be thrown down.”
units.rightText: “Do you see all these things?” He replied. “Truly I tell you, not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.”

units.leftText: As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be? What is the sign of your coming, and of the end of the age?”
units.rightText: While Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to Him privately. “Tell us,” they said, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Be careful that no one leads you astray.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, “See to it that no one deceives you.

units.leftText: For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will lead many astray.
units.rightText: For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.

units.leftText: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
units.rightText: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed. These things must happen, but the end is still to come.

units.leftText: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be famines, plagues, and earthquakes in various places.
units.rightText: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. There will be famines and earthquakes in various places.

units.leftText: But all these things are the beginning of birth pains.
units.rightText: All these are the beginning of birth pains.

units.leftText: “Then they will deliver you up to oppression and will kill you. You will be hated by all of the nations for my name’s sake.
units.rightText: Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.

units.leftText: Then many will stumble, and will deliver up one another, and will hate one another.
units.rightText: At that time many will fall away and will betray and hate one another,

units.leftText: Many false prophets will arise and will lead many astray.
units.rightText: and many false prophets will arise and deceive many.

units.leftText: Because iniquity will be multiplied, the love of many will grow cold.
units.rightText: Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.

units.leftText: But he who endures to the end will be saved.
units.rightText: But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.

units.leftText: This Good News of the Kingdom will be preached in the whole world for a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
units.rightText: And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.

units.leftText: “When, therefore, you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand),
units.rightText: So when you see standing in the holy place ‘the abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by the prophet Daniel (let the reader understand),
rightNotes: 24:15 See Daniel 9:27|DAN 9:27*, Daniel 11:31, and Daniel 12:11.

units.leftText: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
units.rightText: then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.

units.leftText: Let him who is on the housetop not go down to take out the things that are in his house.
units.rightText: Let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve anything from his house.

units.leftText: Let him who is in the field not return back to get his clothes.
units.rightText: And let no one in the field return for his cloak.

units.leftText: But woe to those who are with child and to nursing mothers in those days!
units.rightText: How miserable those days will be for pregnant and nursing mothers!

units.leftText: Pray that your flight will not be in the winter nor on a Sabbath,
units.rightText: Pray that your flight will not occur in the winter or on the Sabbath.

units.leftText: for then there will be great suffering, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, no, nor ever will be.
units.rightText: For at that time there will be great tribulation, unseen from the beginning of the world until now, and never to be seen again.

units.leftText: Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
units.rightText: If those days had not been cut short, nobody would be saved. But for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.

units.leftText: “Then if any man tells you, ‘Behold, here is the Christ!’ or, ‘There!’ don’t believe it.
units.rightText: At that time, if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘There He is!’ do not believe it.

units.leftText: For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will show great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
units.rightText: For false Christs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect, if that were possible.

units.leftText: “Behold, I have told you beforehand.
units.rightText: See, I have told you in advance.

units.leftText: “If therefore they tell you, ‘Behold, he is in the wilderness,’ don’t go out; or ‘Behold, he is in the inner rooms,’ don’t believe it.
units.rightText: So if they tell you, ‘There He is, in the wilderness,’ do not go out, or, ‘Here He is, in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.

units.leftText: For as the lightning flashes from the east, and is seen even to the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
units.rightText: For just as the lightning comes from the east and flashes as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.

units.leftText: For wherever the carcass is, that is where the vultures gather together.
units.rightText: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.

units.leftText: “But immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken;
units.rightText: Immediately after the tribulation of those days:

units.leftText: and then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky. Then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.
units.rightText: At that time the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
rightNotes: 24:30 Or the sky; twice in this verse

units.leftText: He will send out his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather together his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the sky to the other.
units.rightText: And He will send out His angels with a loud trumpet call, and they will gather His elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.

units.leftText: “Now from the fig tree learn this parable: When its branch has now become tender and produces its leaves, you know that the summer is near.
units.rightText: Now learn this lesson from the fig tree: As soon as its branches become tender and sprout leaves, you know that summer is near.
rightNotes: 24:32 Or this parable

units.leftText: Even so you also, when you see all these things, know that he is near, even at the doors.
units.rightText: So also, when you see all these things, you will know that He is near, right at the door.
rightNotes: 24:33 Or it is near

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things are accomplished.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.
leftNotes: 24:34 The word for “generation” (genea) can also be translated as “race.”

units.leftText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
units.rightText: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away.

units.leftText: “But no one knows of that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
units.rightText: No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.
rightNotes: 24:36 BYZ and TR do not include nor the Son.

units.leftText: As the days of Noah were, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
units.rightText: As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

units.leftText: For as in those days which were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noah entered into the ship,
units.rightText: For in the days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.

units.leftText: and they didn’t know until the flood came and took them all away, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
units.rightText: And they were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.

units.leftText: Then two men will be in the field: one will be taken and one will be left.
units.rightText: Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.

units.leftText: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and one will be left.
units.rightText: Two women will be grinding at the mill: one will be taken and the other left.

units.leftText: Watch therefore, for you don’t know in what hour your Lord comes.
units.rightText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.

units.leftText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have watched, and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
units.rightText: But understand this: If the homeowner had known in which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.

units.leftText: Therefore also be ready, for in an hour that you don’t expect, the Son of Man will come.
units.rightText: For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.

units.leftText: “Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has set over his household, to give them their food in due season?
units.rightText: Who then is the faithful and wise servant, whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the proper time?

units.leftText: Blessed is that servant whom his lord finds doing so when he comes.
units.rightText: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

units.leftText: But if that evil servant should say in his heart, ‘My lord is delaying his coming,’
units.rightText: But suppose that servant is wicked and says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’

units.leftText: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eat and drink with the drunkards,
units.rightText: And he begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.

units.leftText: the lord of that servant will come in a day when he doesn’t expect it and in an hour when he doesn’t know it,
units.rightText: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.

units.leftText: and will cut him in pieces and appoint his portion with the hypocrites. That is where the weeping and grinding of teeth will be.
units.rightText: Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the hypocrites, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.[’’]

units.leftText: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
units.rightText: “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.

units.leftText: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
units.rightText: Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.

units.leftText: Those who were foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them,
units.rightText: The foolish ones took their lamps but did not take along any extra oil.

units.leftText: but the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
units.rightText: But the wise ones took oil in flasks along with their lamps.

units.leftText: Now while the bridegroom delayed, they all slumbered and slept.
units.rightText: When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.

units.leftText: But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Behold! The bridegroom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
units.rightText: At midnight the cry rang out: ‘Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!’

units.leftText: Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.
units.rightText: Then all the virgins woke up and trimmed their lamps.
leftNotes: 25:7 The end of the wick of an oil lamp needs to be cut off periodically to avoid having it become clogged with carbon deposits. The wick height is also adjusted so that the flame burns evenly and gives good light without producing a lot of smoke.

units.leftText: The foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
units.rightText: The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil; our lamps are going out.’

units.leftText: But the wise answered, saying, ‘What if there isn’t enough for us and you? You go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
units.rightText: ‘No,’ said the wise ones, ‘or there may not be enough for both us and you. Instead, go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’

units.leftText: While they went away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
units.rightText: But while they were on their way to buy it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.

units.leftText: Afterward the other virgins also came, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us.’
units.rightText: Later the other virgins arrived and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’

units.leftText: But he answered, ‘Most certainly I tell you, I don’t know you.’
units.rightText: But he replied, ‘Truly I tell you, I do not know you.’

units.leftText: Watch therefore, for you don’t know the day nor the hour in which the Son of Man is coming.
units.rightText: Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour.
rightNotes: 25:13 BYZ and TR include when the Son of Man comes.

units.leftText: “For it is like a man going into another country, who called his own servants and entrusted his goods to them.
units.rightText: For it is just like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted them with his possessions.

units.leftText: To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability. Then he went on his journey.
units.rightText: To one he gave five talents, to another two talents, and to another one talent — each according to his own ability. And he went on his journey.
leftNotes: 25:15 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds (usually used to weigh silver unless otherwise specified)
rightNotes: 25:15 A talent was worth about twenty years’ wages for a laborer.

units.leftText: Immediately he who received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents.
units.rightText: The servant who had received the five talents went at once and put them to work and gained five more.
rightNotes: 25:16 Or 15*... And he went on his journey at once. 16*... went and put them to work. Translators vary as to the placement of the Greek adverb eutheōs (at once) at the end of verse 15 or at the beginning of verse 16.

units.leftText: In the same way, he also who got the two gained another two.
units.rightText: Likewise, the one with the two talents gained two more.

units.leftText: But he who received the one talent went away and dug in the earth and hid his lord’s money.
units.rightText: But the servant who had received the one talent went off, dug a hole in the ground, and hid his master’s money.

units.leftText: “Now after a long time the lord of those servants came, and settled accounts with them.
units.rightText: After a long time the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.

units.leftText: He who received the five talents came and brought another five talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents. Behold, I have gained another five talents in addition to them.’
units.rightText: The servant who had received the five talents came and presented five more. ‘Master,’ he said, ‘you entrusted me with five talents. See, I have gained five more.’

units.leftText: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
units.rightText: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

units.leftText: “He also who got the two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents. Behold, I have gained another two talents in addition to them.’
units.rightText: The servant who had received the two talents also came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. See, I have gained two more.’

units.leftText: “His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a few things. I will set you over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’
units.rightText: His master replied, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your master!’

units.leftText: “He also who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you that you are a hard man, reaping where you didn’t sow, and gathering where you didn’t scatter.
units.rightText: Finally, the servant who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man, reaping where you have not sown and gathering where you have not scattered seed.

units.leftText: I was afraid, and went away and hid your talent in the earth. Behold, you have what is yours.’
units.rightText: So I was afraid and went out and hid your talent in the ground. See, you have what belongs to you.’

units.leftText: “But his lord answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant. You knew that I reap where I didn’t sow, and gather where I didn’t scatter.
units.rightText: ‘You wicked, lazy servant!’ replied his master. ‘You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I have not scattered seed.

units.leftText: You ought therefore to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received back my own with interest.
units.rightText: Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and on my return I would have received it back with interest.

units.leftText: Take away therefore the talent from him and give it to him who has the ten talents.
units.rightText: Therefore take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten talents.

units.leftText: For to everyone who has will be given, and he will have abundance, but from him who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away.
units.rightText: For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.

units.leftText: Throw out the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’
units.rightText: And throw that worthless servant into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

units.leftText: “But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
units.rightText: When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on His glorious throne.

units.leftText: Before him all the nations will be gathered, and he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
units.rightText: All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

units.leftText: He will set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left.
units.rightText: He will place the sheep on His right and the goats on His left.

units.leftText: Then the King will tell those on his right hand, ‘Come, blessed of my Father, inherit the Kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world;
units.rightText: Then the King will say to those on His right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by My Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

units.leftText: for I was hungry and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was a stranger and you took me in.
units.rightText: For I was hungry and you gave Me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took Me in,

units.leftText: I was naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me. I was in prison and you came to me.’
units.rightText: I was naked and you clothed Me, I was sick and you looked after Me, I was in prison and you visited Me.’

units.leftText: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
units.rightText: Then the righteous will answer Him, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry and feed You, or thirsty and give You something to drink?

units.leftText: When did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
units.rightText: When did we see You a stranger and take You in, or naked and clothe You?

units.leftText: When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’
units.rightText: When did we see You sick or in prison and visit You?’

units.leftText: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
units.rightText: And the King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers of Mine, you did for Me.’
leftNotes: 25:40 The word for “brothers” here may be also correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Then he will say also to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire which is prepared for the devil and his angels;
units.rightText: Then He will say to those on His left, ‘Depart from Me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

units.leftText: for I was hungry, and you didn’t give me food to eat; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
units.rightText: For I was hungry and you gave Me nothing to eat, I was thirsty and you gave Me nothing to drink,

units.leftText: I was a stranger, and you didn’t take me in; naked, and you didn’t clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
units.rightText: I was a stranger and you did not take Me in, I was naked and you did not clothe Me, I was sick and in prison and you did not look after Me.’

units.leftText: “Then they will also answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and didn’t help you?’
units.rightText: And they too will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see You hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not minister to You?’

units.leftText: “Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you didn’t do it to one of the least of these, you didn’t do it to me.’
units.rightText: Then the King will answer, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for one of the least of these, you did not do for Me.’

units.leftText: These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”
units.rightText: And they will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

units.leftText: When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
units.rightText: When Jesus had finished saying all these things, He told His disciples,

units.leftText: “You know that after two days the Passover is coming, and the Son of Man will be delivered up to be crucified.”
units.rightText: “You know that the Passover is two days away, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”

units.leftText: Then the chief priests, the scribes, and the elders of the people were gathered together in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
units.rightText: At that time the chief priests and elders of the people assembled in the courtyard of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,

units.leftText: They took counsel together that they might take Jesus by deceit and kill him.
units.rightText: and they conspired to arrest Jesus covertly and kill Him.

units.leftText: But they said, “Not during the feast, lest a riot occur among the people.”
units.rightText: “But not during the feast,” they said, “or there may be a riot among the people.”

units.leftText: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
units.rightText: While Jesus was in Bethany in the home of Simon the Leper,
rightNotes: 26:6 Aramaic Simon the Potter or Simon the Jar Maker

units.leftText: a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very expensive ointment, and she poured it on his head as he sat at the table.
units.rightText: a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of expensive perfume, which she poured on His head as He reclined at the table.

units.leftText: But when his disciples saw this, they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
units.rightText: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and asked, “Why this waste?

units.leftText: For this ointment might have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
units.rightText: This perfume could have been sold at a high price, and the money given to the poor.”

units.leftText: However, knowing this, Jesus said to them, “Why do you trouble the woman? She has done a good work for me.
units.rightText: Aware of this, Jesus asked, “Why are you bothering this woman? She has done a beautiful deed to Me.

units.leftText: For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me.
units.rightText: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.
rightNotes: 26:11 See Deuteronomy 15:11|DEU 15:11*.

units.leftText: For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
units.rightText: By pouring this perfume on Me, she has prepared My body for burial.

units.leftText: Most certainly I tell you, wherever this Good News is preached in the whole world, what this woman has done will also be spoken of as a memorial of her.”
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”

units.leftText: Then one of the twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
units.rightText: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

units.leftText: and said, “What are you willing to give me if I deliver him to you?” So they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.
units.rightText: and asked, “What are you willing to give me if I hand Him over to you?” And they set out for him thirty pieces of silver.

units.leftText: From that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
units.rightText: So from then on Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.

units.leftText: Now on the first day of unleavened bread, the disciples came to Jesus, saying to him, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
units.rightText: On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?”
rightNotes: 26:17 Literally On the first of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: He said, “Go into the city to a certain person, and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is at hand. I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
units.rightText: He answered, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him that the Teacher says, ‘My time is near. I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house.’”

units.leftText: The disciples did as Jesus commanded them, and they prepared the Passover.
units.rightText: So the disciples did as Jesus had directed them and prepared the Passover.

units.leftText: Now when evening had come, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
units.rightText: When evening came, Jesus was reclining with the twelve disciples.
rightNotes: 26:20 BYZ and TR the Twelve

units.leftText: As they were eating, he said, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
units.rightText: And while they were eating, He said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”

units.leftText: They were exceedingly sorrowful, and each began to ask him, “It isn’t me, is it, Lord?”
units.rightText: They were deeply grieved and began to ask Him one after another, “Surely not I, Lord?”

units.leftText: He answered, “He who dipped his hand with me in the dish will betray me.
units.rightText: Jesus answered, “The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me.

units.leftText: The Son of Man goes even as it is written of him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would be better for that man if he had not been born.”
units.rightText: The Son of Man will go just as it is written about Him, but woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born.”

units.leftText: Judas, who betrayed him, answered, “It isn’t me, is it, Rabbi?”
units.rightText: Then Judas, who would betray Him, said, “Surely not I, Rabbi?”

units.leftText: As they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks for it, and broke it. He gave to the disciples and said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
units.rightText: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is My body.”
leftNotes: 26:26 TR reads “blessed” instead of “gave thanks for”

units.leftText: He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave to them, saying, “All of you drink it,
units.rightText: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.

units.leftText: for this is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins.
units.rightText: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
rightNotes: 26:28 BYZ and TR the new covenant

units.leftText: But I tell you that I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on, until that day when I drink it anew with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
units.rightText: I tell you, I will not drink of this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom.”

units.rightText: “Do not be afraid,” said Jesus. “Go and tell My brothers to go to Galilee. There they will see Me.”
leftNotes: 28:10 The word for “brothers” here may be also correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
units.rightText: While the women were on their way, some of the guards went into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened.

units.leftText: When they were assembled with the elders and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
units.rightText: And after the chief priests had met with the elders and formed a plan, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money

units.leftText: saying, “Say that his disciples came by night and stole him away while we slept.
units.rightText: and instructed them: “You are to say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole Him away while we were asleep.’

units.leftText: If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
units.rightText: If this report reaches the governor, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble.”

units.leftText: So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
units.rightText: So the guards took the money and did as they were instructed. And this account has been circulated among the Jews to this very day.

units.leftText: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
units.rightText: Meanwhile, the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had designated.

units.leftText: When they saw him, they bowed down to him; but some doubted.
units.rightText: When they saw Him, they worshiped Him, but some doubted.

units.leftText: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
units.rightText: Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me.

units.leftText: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
rightNotes: 28:19 Literally Having gone, therefore, make disciples

units.leftText: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.
units.rightText: and teaching them to obey all that I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
